title: Data leakage
content:
## We treat your data with the same care you would

When you build on Emergent, you're trusting us with app code, database records, API keys, and sometimes sensitive business logic. We've architected every layer of the platform to prevent accidental exposure or leakage.

<Callout type="success" title="Your data stays yours">
Emergent does **not** train AI models on your code, prompts, or database content. We do not share your project data with third parties outside the AI providers required to run agents and generate media. Your secrets, database records, and deployed apps remain isolated to your workspace.
</Callout>

---

## What gets sent to AI providers

Emergent uses third-party language models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) to power agents and Wingman. Here's what those providers see:

| Data type | Sent to AI | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| Your chat messages & prompts | Yes | Instruction and context for the agent |
| Generated code files | Yes | So the agent can read, edit, and reason about your app |
| Database schema | Yes | To help the agent write queries and understand data structure |
| Database **records** | Only if you explicitly paste them into chat | Agent needs to see sample data to debug or build features |
| Environment variable **names** | Yes | Agent can reference `process.env.STRIPE_KEY` in code |
| Environment variable **values** | **No** | Secrets are injected at runtime; agents never see the actual API key |
| Job & deployment logs (stdout/stderr) | Partially | If the agent is debugging a failing build, recent logs may be included in context |

<Note>
AI providers process this data to respond to your request but—per their terms—do not train public models on API traffic from enterprise/commercial use.
</Note>

---

## Secrets & environment variables

When you add an API key or secret in the **Env** panel, it is:

- Encrypted at rest in our database
- Injected into your app's runtime **only** (not visible in code)
- Never included in chat context sent to the AI

The agent can *write* code that references `process.env.YOUR_SECRET`, but it never sees the plaintext value. This prevents accidental logging, copy-paste errors, or model memorization.

<Warning>
If you **paste** a secret directly into the chat (e.g., "use API key `sk-12345…`"), that text *will* be sent to the AI provider. Always add secrets via the Env panel instead.
</Warning>

---

## Database isolation

Every Emergent workspace includes a dedicated MongoDB instance. Your database is:

- **Not shared** across workspaces or users
- Accessible only via the platform's scoped connection (the agent and your deployed app)
- Encrypted in transit and at rest

The agent can read and write collections to build features, but it does not have shell access or admin privileges beyond standard CRUD operations.

<Tip>
If you're connecting an **external** database (via a connection string in Env), standard network security applies—ensure you've whitelisted Emergent's IP range and use credentials with least-privilege access.
</Tip>

---

## Code & deployment artifacts

All source code, build logs, and deployment artifacts live in isolated storage tied to your workspace. Emergent staff do not browse your code unless you explicitly grant support access during a troubleshooting session.

Your app is deployed to a sandboxed container with:

- Ephemeral filesystem (writes don't persist between jobs)
- No access to other users' processes or data
- Rate-limited egress to prevent abuse

<Info>
Deployed apps are publicly accessible by URL, so **do not hard-code sensitive data** in client-side JavaScript or HTML. Use environment variables and server-side logic to protect secrets.
</Info>

---

## What we log & retain

Emergent retains:

- **Chat transcripts** – to preserve your workspace history and allow agents to reference past context
- **Job run metadata** – timestamps, credit usage, stop reasons
- **Error logs** – to help you (and us) debug failed builds

We do **not** retain:

- Full HTTP request/response bodies from your deployed app
- Database query results (beyond what the agent writes to the DB itself)
- Media files uploaded by your app's end users (unless you explicitly store them in your own MongoDB or external storage)

<Callout type="note" title="Data retention for troubleshooting">
If you delete a workspace, all associated code, chat history, and database records are **permanently removed** within 30 days. Aggregated usage metrics (credit spend, job count) are retained for billing and analytics but are not tied to identifiable project content.
</Callout>

---

## Compliance & best practices

While Emergent is designed for rapid prototyping and production-grade apps, you remain responsible for:

- **Not storing PII or regulated data** (HIPAA, PCI DSS) unless you've architected appropriate safeguards (encryption, access controls) in your own app logic
- **Reviewing generated code** for accidental logging of secrets or sensitive user data
- **Using environment variables** for all API keys, database credentials, and OAuth secrets

<Tip>
For production apps handling sensitive data, consider adding a middleware layer (auth tokens, field-level encryption) in your app code. Emergent gives you full control over your stack—use it to enforce your own security policies.
</Tip>

---

## Reporting a concern

If you believe your data has been exposed or you've discovered a vulnerability, email **security@emergent.ai** immediately. We triage security reports within 24 hours and will work with you to remediate any confirmed issues.

For general data or privacy questions, see our **Privacy Policy** (linked in the workspace footer) or reach out to support via the in-app chat.
description: Safeguards against leakage; what is / isn't exposed and how it's protected.
